chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
He was asked about Dhihar (expiation by declaring oneself like the mother's back) upon a free woman and a slave woman; he said: Yes.

key_terms.الظَّهَار: Dhihar, a form of divorce in Islamic jurisprudence where a husband declares his wife to his back.

ai.seo_question: Does the ruling of Dhihar apply to slave women as well as free women?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in *al-Istibsar* confirms the applicability of Dhihar (conjugal expiation) to both free and slave women, highlighting the Imam's affirmation of legal parity in this specific ruling. It underscores the consistency of Shia jurisprudence in extending the obligations of Dhihar across social strata, as recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi in Chapter 161. The brevity of the report emphasizes the established nature of this ruling within the Imami school.
